prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every situation — the right choice depends on your budget, the type of roof/materials you want, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and the neighborhood. I can, however, help you find the best company for your needs and give you the checklist to choose confidently.

If you want, I can look up top-rated roofers near you now — tell me your Dallas ZIP code or neighborhood. Otherwise, use the guidance below to find and vet contractors.

How to find top roofers in Dallas
- Search local reviews on Google Maps, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor and Nextdoor.
- Use manufacturer “find a contractor” tools (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) to find certified contractors in Dallas.
- Ask neighbors or HOA for recent recommendations and to see finished roofs in person.
- Get at least 3 written estimates for comparison.

What to verify before hiring
- Insurance: Ask for certificates of liability insurance and workers’ compensation. Call the insurer to verify coverage.
- Local registration/permitting: Texas has no statewide roofing license, but many Dallas-area cities require registration/permits — confirm the contractor knows local permit requirements and will pull permits.
- References and portfolio: Request recent local references and photos of completed roof replacements.
- Certifications: Look for manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster) — those often indicate training and warranties.
- Warranties: Get both the manufacturer’s material warranty and the contractor’s workmanship warranty in writing (length and what it covers).
- Written contract: Should include scope of work, materials (brand/model/color), start and completion dates, payment schedule, cleanup/disposal, and lien waiver provision.
- Payment terms: Avoid paying large upfront sums. Typical deposit patterns vary, but a very large upfront payment is a red flag.

Questions to ask each contractor
- How long have you been working in the Dallas area?
- Can you show proof of insurance and local registration/permits?
- Who will do the work — your employees or subs?
- What brand and class of shingles do you recommend and why?
- What warranties do you offer (workmanship and manufacturer)?
- Will you handle insurance claims and meet the adjuster on site?
- Do you provide a written, itemized estimate and contract?

Red flags
- Door-to-door storm-chaser salespeople pressuring you to sign immediately.
- No local physical address or unwillingness to provide references.
- Refuses to provide proof of insurance, permits, or a written contract.
- Requests full payment upfront or only accepts cash.

Typical costs and timeline (ballpark)
- Costs vary widely by roof size, pitch, materials, and tear-off or overlay. In Dallas, full replacement for an average single-family home commonly ranges widely — always get local estimates.
- Replacements typically take 1–3 days for a normal-sized house (plus time for inspections/permits).

Next step
If you want, give me your ZIP code or address and I’ll pull a short list (3–5) of highly rated Dallas roofers and summarize their strengths and what to watch for.
